ctx.x: His name was, uh, Jack Bunch. And he was with the band that Woody Herman started with in New Orleans at Club Forest in 1932. It was called Tom Guerinovich. Yeah. Later shortened to Tom Guerin. And his band, they were from San Francisco. Very popular in New Orleans. And, uh, anybody who played at Club Forest was popular, I'll tell you that. Ben Pollock played there. Yeah. And, uh, I visited Jack there. Snoozer Quinn, of course, was a big friend of mine. He was in New Orleans at the time. But, uh, tricks were all…
Who did Ezell play with in New York?

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: that is the year that the Ben Pollack Band played Club Forrest in New Orleans.

ctx.x: Just so I can see what's happening here. I'm trying to figure out how to prop it out. That's okay. Go ahead. It's facing you.

Okay. There was a music store in 3-4th, formed by Bubba Broyles. Bubba was a trumpet player, and he'd been playing with the local bands there. And, he was a great friend of Mr. A.J. LaCoste, who was a power with the Whirland Organization. A.J. was the management of the band department. He organized school bands all over Mississippi and Louisiana. He was a tremendous man. But, Bubba and LaCoste asked me to come to New Orleans, that I would have some kind of a job. I had, I tried to go back to playing and played…
You have to be careful. Now you were talking about Leslie Nurse, was his name?
